title: Google designs private cloud memory for personal AI
friendlyTitle: Google wants AI memory to stay private
summary: Google has detailed a Private AI Compute architecture for persistent, cross-device assistant memory. It combines encrypted per-user storage, device-held keys and secure cloud enclaves, with software verification and an independent security audit.
friendlySummary: Google described a way for an AI assistant to remember information across your devices. Your devices would keep the keys, while protected cloud computers would briefly open the data only when needed.
whyItMatters: Long-term memory could make assistants far more useful, but it also concentrates sensitive context. Google’s design shows the technical direction to watch: continuity across devices without giving the service operator routine access to the stored data.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A helpful assistant may need memory, but personal information needs strong protection. This design tries to provide both.
